releases.name: v1.0.0: opencode tool backend
releases.body:
## Highlights

- Opencode tool backend, opt-in via OPENCODE_MUSE_TOOL_BACKEND (#37): private per-session config, loopback MCP bridge, parked-call attach. Default muse backend unchanged. Proven with a live turn per backend plus fail-closed setup.
- Rewind/fork on the pinned Muse 1.4.14 runtime (#20): anchor ledger, explicit-cut fork, fail-closed unmappable rewinds.
- Registry lifecycle (#49) and loopback hardening (#50) found by adversarial review, fixed before release.

## Gate

tsc clean, full suite green on both backends, probe:host-override ok on 1.4.14. Requires Muse Code 1.4.14 and @muse-code/sdk 1.4.14.

## Known limitations

- #36: no sampling support in the pinned runtime.
- #35: no responseFormat support in the pinned runtime.
- #22: provider approval UX waits on upstream OpenCode core support.
- #6: open UI issue, waiting on upstream.

See docs/compatibility.md for pins, probe results, and details.

## What is new since 0.8.0

- Rewind/fork re-enabled on the pinned Muse 1.4.14 runtime (tracks #20): rewinding the OpenCode conversation forks the mapped Muse session at the retained turn boundary via an explicit cut point; unmappable boundaries keep the fail-closed fresh-session error. OpenCode forks with a uniquely matching transcript adopt via fork instead of starting blank.
- Forks do not preserve source turn ids (offline probe check 4b): re-pointed entries drop anchors and post-fork turns re-anchor; the fork's own turns stay forkable.
- Rewinding never rolls back files Muse changed, and every rewind orphans the pre-rewind Muse session in the user's Muse home (MSP has no delete).

Strict build, 368/368 tests, and offline probe (override, rawLog, resume, fork, fork-of-fork, steer) pass. Install snippet pinned to 0.9.0 in the same commit (lockstep rule).

## What is new since 0.7.1

- Muse CLI and @muse-code/sdk are both pinned to 1.4.14: the SDK expected fingerprint equals the served stable fingerprint, so exact-pin equality is restored and no startup warning is recorded (tracks #47).
- Schema delta 1.4.13 -> 1.4.14 classified additive-only; snapshot ledger verified against a fresh export.
- Steering (#44), per-model thinking levels (#45), and lease drainer counting (#48) now run against the matching SDK.
- Probe helper accepts -32030 commandRejected as rename-unavailable alongside the old -32603.

Strict build, 358/358 tests, offline probe all true. Live catalog, text turn, and explicit-cut fork PASS on subscription and PAYG (user-reported keyed-shell runs). Install snippet pinned to 0.8.0 in the same commit (lockstep rule).

Patch release: approval-bridge reliability fixes, all verified live against OpenCode 2.1.3.

- Fix conversational deny-loop trap: after a second unrecognized answer the denial stands, the parked turn is interrupted, and the message runs as a fresh turn, so a re-asking model can never trap the conversation.
- Recovery choice (\#38) defers to live bindings: no more false recovery prompts on slow turn/start; the turn-lifecycle rule decides in resolve.
- Verdicts are consumed before session resolve and matched against the latest user message only, fixing WorkspaceBusyError deadlocks and stale-text joins.
- Park wire-object approval requirement ids under the canonical key, fixing the round where every approval was unroutable.
- Retry worktree-bearing session/start once on explicit rejection (non-git/SVN/plain checkouts).
- Funnel all usage through nested V3 containers, fixing the flat-usage crash.
- Brief the model against prose permission asks (\#39), ending the double approval prompt.
- Derive Allow/Deny labels when the CLI offers no presentable options.

releases.name: v0.7.0: per-session worktrees
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.6.0

- Each OpenCode session starts its Muse session on a server-managed worktree instead of sharing the checkout, so concurrent sessions stop serializing at the workspace lock (tracks #34, which stays open for the remaining lease-protocol and orphans work).
- The human merges through normal source control; the bridge never auto-merges, and purge-on-close removes only provably-empty worktrees.
- Graceful fallback: untrusted workspaces and CLIs without the experimental surface keep the single-writer lock with a conversational notice.
- First-turn labels tell the agent which worktree it is on; PDF staging follows the session onto its worktree.

Strict build, 310/310 tests, and package-contents checks pass. Install snippet pinned to 0.7.0 in the same commit (lockstep rule).
